name: Glucomannan
short: Trials report abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea and constipation. A case report describes oesophageal obstruction from a swelling glucomannan diet aid; it may alter absorption of other medicines.
text: In a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials of glucomannan in overweight and obese people, the adverse events reported included abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea and constipation. Glucomannan absorbs water and expands rapidly to many times its original size, and a case report describes a 37-year-old woman who developed delayed oesophageal obstruction after taking a non-prescription diet aid containing glucomannan; she was later found to have an oesophageal web, and the authors concluded that the case illustrates the potential dangers of glucomannan in people with a history of upper gastrointestinal disease. The same report lists flatulence, abdominal pain, gastrointestinal obstruction and possible modification of the bioavailability of other medications among the negative effects reported; no specific medicines were named.
